records.text: Frank Turek cited Deuteronomy 19 as prescribing the penalty for a crime against someone found to have falsely accused another person of that crime.
records.speaker: Frank Turek

appearances.snippet: Deuteronomy 19 in the Old Testament economy says if you accuse somebody falsely of a crime and you're found out, you get the penalty of that crime.

verification.notes: The transcript at 270.58 seconds records Turek citing Deuteronomy 19 for the proposition that a proven false accuser receives the penalty intended for the accused. Deuteronomy 19:16-21 states that judges must investigate and do to a false witness what the witness intended to do to the accused. Turek's summary omits the passage's judicial-process setting but accurately conveys the cited rule.
